summary: Kickoff for Redwood onboarding with Horizon Bridge. Aligned on scope (staging then prod), security requirements (SAML, KMS, audit logs), performance goals, and next steps for staging tenant and initial benchmarks. Decided to run a small pilot for NLG customer-support flows, then expand to embeddings search use case.
topics: initial performance benchmarks and KV caching
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-21 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Rita Alvarez (CSM), Lena Ortiz (Horizon Head of ML), Samir Patel (Platform Eng), Joan Kim (Security), Alex Dray (SRE)

---
00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um this is maya with redwood inference, i'm the AE on the account. quick roll call?
00:12 Lena: hi lena here, head of ml at horizon bridge.
00:16 Samir: samir, platform eng.
00:19 Joan: joan, security.
00:21 Alex: alex, s r e.
00:24 Ethan: ethan from redwood, i'll be the technical se for the onboarding.
00:28 Maya: cool, objective today is to walk through the onramp plan, confirm security and networking needs, and schedule the staging provisioning. we'll also plan a quick perf baseline for the pilot.

02:05 Maya: high level, horizon wants to run two initial workloads: one is an NLG customer support assistant in staging, and the other is embeddings for internal search. is that right, lena?
02:18 Lena: yeah that's right, we want to validate latency and cost numbers first on the NLG flows because those are the priority for q1.
02:33 Samir: timeline wise we're hoping to have staging in place next week, and a pilot with our service team in the first half of december.

04:10 Ethan: ok great. On the infra side we'll provision a staging tenant in the redwood console, by default it's hosted, but we can set up a dedicated pool if you want reserved capacity. just to clarify: are you leaning hosted or dedicated for the pilot?
04:25 Samir: for pilot we prefer hosted to move faster, but for prod we probably need dedicated because of predictable throughput and isolation.
04:36 Joan: security note: we need SAML S S O with SCIM, full audit logs, and customer-managed keys - or at least integration with our KMS. also data residency question — our EU customers' data needs to stay in eu-west.
04:54 Maya: yep we support SAML and SCIM, and we have KMS integrations. we'll send the security pack after this call. for residency we have region options and can pin model clusters to eu-west.

06:30 Ethan: on the runtime side, a few things to call out: caching of KV/cash — the KV cache helps reduce repeated context cost. our engine supports continuous batching and we can tune batching windows to balance latency vs throughput.
06:50 Lena: can you explain the KV cache behavior? we have multi-turn conversations and can't afford token mismatches.
07:05 Ethan: sure, so we keep a per-session KV cache, it's -- normally transparent but you can opt in to prefix caching. sometimes in the transcript people say K V cash which is funny in the logs, but yeah it's per-session and we expose hooks for eviction.

10:14 Samir: network questions: we want VPC peering and strict egress controls, can redwood support private deployments or do we need dedicated?
10:28 Maya: we have Redwood Private and Dedicated. Redwood Private is the VPC/on-prem option with private control plane. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools but still managed. For strict VPC peering and no public egress, Private is the right fit. For pilot though, VPC peering to a staging VPC is doable with limited setup.
10:50 Joan: audit trail — we need immutable audit logs retained for 12 months and SSO mappings to roles. is there RBAC that ties into SCIM groups?
11:05 Ethan: yes, we map SCIM groups to roles in the console. Audit logs are available and can be shipped to your SIEM; retention is an enterprise add-on but we can enable 12-month retention based on the support tier.

13:00 Alex: perf baseline — what metrics should we measure in the first run?
13:08 Ethan: latency p95, token cost per call, throughput (requests per second), and cold-start behavior for long sequences. Also memory/KV cache hit rates.
13:22 Maya: and we'll include cost projections using the Optimize toolkit suggestions — quantization and batching profiles for your expected token length.

16:45 Lena: on models: do you have a vetted model list? we're currently testing a mix of open LLMs. we want deterministic-ish responses for support templates.
16:58 Ethan: we have a model catalog with redwood-verified performance. for determinism you can pin temperature and use structured output or function calls. also we can recommend quantized variants if you'd like lower cost.

20:02 Samir: integration concerns: our infra uses k8s and a service mesh, any constraints we should know about?
20:12 Ethan: for private deployments we'd run the runtime in your VPC/on-prem; for hosted, the integration is via the API with short-lived keys. If you want to run egress through your mesh, we can work through the networking doc but typically you won't run Redwood's runtime inside your cluster unless choosing on-prem.

24:00 Joan: compliance checklist — SOC two, ISO 27001 evidence, pen test reports. can you provide those?
24:12 Maya: yes we'll attach SOC 2 and ISO docs. note: in the past we've had the doc title come through as S O C two in some transcripts, that's not a live issue, just transcription.

27:45 Lena: data retention and deletion: what are the guarantees on logs and prompts?
27:54 Ethan: we have config for request retention and an option to disable prompt logging on the hosted tier; for enterprise/private you can opt out and keep logs within your environment. We'll share the retention matrix.

31:10 Samir: ok so next actions — provisioning and access. what do you need from us?
31:18 Maya: SSO metadata (SAML), SCIM group mapping, a list of IP ranges for VPC peering if you want to set that up, and a point of contact for the SRE access.
31:34 Alex: i'll send the IP ranges and an invite for our onboarding SRE.
31:40 Joan: i'll compile the compliance Qs and send them to maya.

34:00 Ethan: i'll spin up the staging tenant and seed a small model for the NLG pilot. i'll need kube creds if we do on-prem but for hosted it's just API keys.
34:12 Samir: we'll aim for hosted staging this week. if you can provide the staging URL and keys, we'll run a smoke test.

38:00 Maya: pitfalls and lessons from other customers: don't push to prod without load-testing, and validate batch sizes on your traffic profile — we've seen cost go up when defaults were not tuned. also watch out for tokenization differences across open models.
38:28 Lena: good to know.

41:10 Alex: curious about fallback/deg degrade strategies — if a model is overloaded, can we fallback to smaller variant automatically?
41:21 Ethan: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies. you can configure a policy to route to a cheaper/compatible variant or to a cached response, and things like timeouts and canary rollouts are supported from the console.

44:00 Joan: encryption in transit and at rest? do you support customer-managed keys for model weights?
44:12 Maya: encryption in transit is standard TLS, at rest we support KMS integrations for request logs and stored artifacts. For model weights, in private deployments you can control the storage layer. For hosted, we use provider-managed secure storage but can enable bring-your-own-keys where supported.

48:30 Lena: any blockers we should expect for the pilot?
48:38 Maya: the common blockers are SAML metadata mismatch, IP ranges not provisioned for peering, and missing SCIM group definitions. we'll share a quick preflight checklist.

51:00 Maya: recap — action items: maya sends onboarding runbook and security pack; ethan provisions staging and shares keys; samir/alex to give IP ranges and SRE contact; joan to send compliance Qs. schedule perf baseline for week of 11-30. Does that capture it?
51:20 Samir: yes.
51:23 Joan: yes, sounds good.
51:30 Lena: thanks everyone, excited to get started.
52:05 Maya: awesome, i'll follow up with calendar invites and the runbook. thanks all.
